meta.name: Floor Task List
meta.source: app/screens/TasksScreen.jsx, Protrack (Milaca Meats), captured live via localhost:3100, 2026-09-03
meta.medium_of_origin: web app screen (React/Tailwind), touch-density fork for tablet floor terminals
not_copied: the specific task copy ("Restock Applewood Bacon" etc.) — content, not system
meta.note: This screen is an application of the existing `.claude/skills/notion/` DNA, not a competing system. This spec records only what is SPECIFIC to the task-list pattern — category sectioning, row interaction model, tabbed segmented filter with count dots, sticky toolbar transition, add/edit modal — layered on top of the Notion base (font stack, control height, accent budget, warm neutrals, hairline rules all still apply and are not re-derived here).
meta.primitives: StickyFadeHeader, SectionHeading and RowActions in app/components/ui.jsx carry this spec's toolbar, section-heading and row-action rules. Use them rather than re-inlining the markup.
meta.applied_to: Restyled onto all eight other list screens 2026-09-03 (floor Team/Inventory; console Team/Locations/Stations/Permissions/Integrations/Inventory), verified live at desktop and touch.
meta.scope_warning: Measured off one dense GROUPED list. 'No card borders, hairlines only' is safe here only because section headings are the containing device. On a flat list of peers with no grouping dimension, dropping the container leaves rows floating with no edge — worse, not cleaner. Rule: rule a grouped list, box a flat one (Card is border-y only, so boxing a flat list does not break the ban on wrapping a GROUP in a box).

soul.one_line: A checklist that reads as a ledger: ruled category sections, one accent color spent on exactly one next action, rows that toggle by tapping anywhere.
soul.lineage: Notion database view crossed with a paper clipboard checklist
soul.read_distance: arm's length on a mounted tablet, not a desk monitor — must hold up at ~50-70cm

colors.hex: warm red, same pill shape/opacity recipe as amber
colors.name: red pill

banned_behaviours: no second accent color for a second 'kind' of action — only ONE task-list button (New task) and ONE tab-selection wash get color-or-tint treatment
never tint a whole row for priority — priority lives only in the small pill, never as a row background
never color a checkbox or checkmark anything but ink + the one accent-adjacent 'ok' tone used app-wide

scale.display_to_body_ratio: 2:1 (28px page title vs 14px body — this screen does NOT use the full 2.3:1 app max, title sits one notch down from the app's largest)
steps_used_on_this_screen: 12px (meta line, category label, priority pill, tab label secondary state)
14px (task title, tab label active, button label)
28px (page title, only place larger than 14px appears)

treatment.tracking: category section label is +tracked and uppercase — the ONE place on this screen text is uppercased; everything else is sentence case
treatment.leading: tight, ~1.1, rows are height-driven by padding not line-height
treatment.case: uppercase ONLY for category section headers; everything else sentence case, never title case
treatment.numerals: tabular where counts appear (dots, priority text stays word not number)

space.grid: single column list, no grid — hierarchy comes from section > row > row-detail nesting, not columns
space.margin_pct: content column caps ~700px in a wider canvas; on tablet it runs edge-to-edge with ~16-24px side padding
space.gutter_pct: row internal padding 12px vertical / 4px horizontal; section-to-section gap one blank line's worth (~16-20px) plus the rule
space.alignment: left-aligned throughout, no centering except the empty-state and modal, which center on the viewport
space.rhythm: section heading -> its rows (pl-6, nested left) -> hairline hand-off to next section heading, no card boundary anywhere
space.negative_space: generous vertical breathing room between rows (12px) but zero horizontal margin around the list — it runs the full content width
space.safe_area: sticky toolbar (tabs + New task + settings) always visible; content scrolls under it, never the reverse

surface.edges: 1px hairline rules only, never a box, except the New-task/Edit-task modal which is the one true bordered surface
surface.elevation: nothing at rest has a shadow; the modal is the only elevated surface (backdrop dim + itself)
surface.imagery: none — no icons except: one small lucide glyph per category (leading its heading), a decorative checkbox square, and Pencil/Trash2 on hover
surface.iconography: 12-16px lucide icons only, always ink-3 or ink-2, never colored except the count dot and priority pill

signatures.move: Category sectioning, always, never a flat list
signatures.how: every tab (Open, Yours, Due today, Overdue, Completed) buckets its rows into category headings, each an icon + uppercase label + count + a hairline rule running out to the right edge on the heading's own line
signatures.when: on every tab with any content, including a tab that only has one category present that day
signatures.never: collapse to a flat unheaded list just because only one category is present — this was tried and explicitly rejected

signatures.how: the entire row (title + note + meta) is the toggle target, not just a checkbox — role=button on the <li> itself
signatures.when: every row, every tab, including Completed (toggles back to open)
signatures.never: make the checkbox the only hit target — the decorative square is a status indicator, not a control

signatures.how: edit (pencil) and delete (trash) icons sit at opacity-0, fade to opacity-100 on row hover or keyboard focus, positioned right-aligned
signatures.when: any pointer device. On touch (`hover: none`) they must be FORCED visible instead — there is no hover to reveal them, and reaching them via focus means first tapping the row, which on a row that is itself a button fires that row's action instead.
signatures.never: show edit/delete permanently on a hover-capable device — they'd compete with the tap-to-toggle target; and never leave them hover-only, which makes them unreachable on the tablet floor terminals this app actually runs on

signatures.move: Segmented tab row with a badge dot, not a filter dropdown
signatures.how: five tabs (Open/Yours/Due today/Overdue/Completed) rendered as a Segmented control, each carrying a small numeric count in a filled circular badge
signatures.when: top of the screen, always visible, sticky
signatures.never: hide tab counts behind a hover or a secondary click — the count is the point, it's a floor triage tool

signatures.move: One line of meta per row, icon-prefixed, ink-3
signatures.how: assignee icon + 'Anyone on shift' or a name, calendar icon + due-date phrase (color-coded only when overdue/due-today), 'Assigned by X' trailing — all one line, all 12px ink-3, wrapping to two lines only accepted overflow
signatures.never: let meta compete with the title in size or weight — it is always the quietest text in the row

signatures.move: Priority as a pill, never as row color
signatures.how: a small rounded-full 12px/500 pill sits inline after the title, only rendered for High/Urgent (Normal/Low get no pill at all — absence is the signal for 'ordinary')
signatures.when: task.priority is High or Urgent only
signatures.never: give Normal or Low priority any visual marker — a marker for 'normal' would be noise

signatures.move: Sticky toolbar that fades its own bottom edge
signatures.how: the toolbar carries `mask-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, black 0, black calc(100% - 18px), transparent 100%)` on ITSELF, with its own bottom padding (44px) holding the fade zone. A mask only controls this box's alpha, so it fades whatever background the bar really has without a second element hand-matched per breakpoint, needs no JS 'am I stuck yet' state, and contributes its height to the scroller's natural scrollHeight so nothing below needs a matching reserve.
signatures.when: any tab with enough rows to scroll
signatures.never: paint a separate absolutely-positioned gradient strip below the bar (the superseded approach — it needed a per-breakpoint colour match and a hand-tuned reserve on the content below), and never use a plain opaque-to-transparent gradient, which reveals legible text at its own top edge

weird_move.move: The checkbox is not a button.
weird_move.how: the visible checkbox square is an aria-hidden decorative <span> — it looks exactly like a real checkbox control (bordered square, fills with a check when done) but has zero click handling of its own. The click handler lives on the entire row. A user who carefully aims for 'the checkbox' and a user who taps anywhere in the row get the identical result — the UI shows a familiar control affordance while deliberately not requiring the precision it implies.
weird_move.never: add a real onClick to the checkbox span specifically, or stop the row's onClick from firing when the checkbox area is tapped — that would silently break the whole-row-tap contract this screen depends on for glove-handed floor use

archetypes.purpose: the main view: sticky toolbar + category-sectioned rows for whichever tab is active
archetypes.anatomy: page title -> sticky[Segmented tabs w/ count dots, New task button (manager only), Settings icon button] -> repeat[category heading -> ul of rows] -> optional back-to-top button
archetypes.content_shape: 0-N categories, each with 1-N rows; empty tab shows a centered empty state, not a blank white rectangle

archetypes.anatomy: decorative checkbox span -> title (+ optional priority pill inline) -> optional note line (bold 'Note:' label + text) -> meta line (assignee, due date, assigned-by) -> hover-revealed edit/trash icons
archetypes.content_shape: title required; note, due date, priority pill, assignee, completed-by all optional and independently absent

archetypes.anatomy: centered card, hairline border, on dimmed backdrop: title bar (icon + 'New task'/'Edit task' + close X) -> stacked labeled fields (text input, category pill-select, priority pill-select, assign-to pill-select, date input, note input) -> footer[Cancel ghost button, primary Add/Save button right-aligned]
archetypes.content_shape: same field set for create and edit; edit pre-fills every field and swaps the header/button chrome only

motion.easing: default browser ease, nothing custom-tuned observed on this screen
motion.durations: opacity fades (hover-reveal actions, toolbar skirt) read as fast/instant, no springy or slow transitions
motion.entrances: no enter animation on rows or modal beyond the browser's own
motion.never_moves: rows never reorder with an animated transition — a toggle instantly re-sorts (open-first) with no shuffle motion
motion.reduced_motion: safe by default — nothing here depends on motion for meaning

voice.register: plant-floor plain: short imperative task titles ('Restock Applewood Bacon on the floor', 'Face and rotate the jerky case'), notes are one practical sentence
voice.sentence_length: titles under ~8 words; notes under ~20 words

bans: never wrap a row or a category section in a bordered card — sections are separated by hairline rules only
never use a second accent color; the blue belongs to exactly one action per screen
never color a whole row for priority or status — color lives only in the small pill
never make the checkbox itself the sole click target — the row is the target
never show row actions (edit/delete) at rest on desktop — hover/focus-reveal only
never collapse category sectioning to a flat list even with a single category present
never introduce a drop shadow at rest — only the modal gets elevation, and even then it's a dim backdrop, not a shadow stack
never give 'Normal' or 'Low' priority a visible marker
never exceed 4 distinct type sizes on the screen at once
never leave a hover-revealed control hover-only — under `hover: none` it must be forced visible, or it cannot be reached at all

tests.test: no category section is ever rendered as a bare <ul> without its icon+label+count+rule heading, even with one category present
exactly one primary-blue filled control is visible per screen state (the New task button or the active-tab wash never both read as 'primary' at once)
a resting row shows zero edit/delete icon opacity; a hovered/focused row shows full opacity
checkbox span has no independent click handler; clicking it fires the same toggle as clicking the row
priority pill is present only when priority is High or Urgent; absent for Normal/Low
meta line is always 12px and always the lightest ink color on the row (never darker than the title)
no row, section, or list is wrapped in a border-radius > 0 container other than pills and the modal
type sizes present on screen at once number 4 or fewer
category heading text is uppercase; no other text on the screen is uppercase
the sticky toolbar carries its own mask-image fade; no separate gradient strip element exists
under `hover: none`, every row-action group computes to opacity 1

reconstruction.method: measured directly from the running app (Playwright against a live `next dev` build of TasksScreen.jsx) rather than blind-rebuilt from a written spec — ground truth, not a reconstruction diff
gaps_found: exact px row height varies with content (66-89px with a note vs ~40px without) — recorded as a range, not a fixed token
priority pill border-radius resolved to a huge px value from Tailwind's rounded-full — recorded as 'pill/fully-rounded' rather than a literal number
